visual_review_scope: Reference token and surrounding source-verse callout are checked from the original 821x1162 print page. The printed book frequently contains a longer grouped apparatus than a single digital xt; no statement that the entire USFX xt text is the literal printed note is implied.

records.clarification: The actual printed Genesis 9:4 blood prohibition is linked by an x-style marginal note to Leviticus 7:26. The eBible full note includes that target after an unaddressable Leviticus 3:27, but the complete eBible `xt` sequence is not a verbatim printed margin and remains unapproved for machine links.

The original printed Genesis 35:10 renaming of Jacob to Israel uses the b marginal same-book reference 'voy. 32. 28.' corresponding to Genesis 32:28. The additional eBible/second-digital 2 Chronicles 17 target cannot be certified from this printed note.

The original printed Leviticus 16:27 marginal group includes Hebrews 13:11 alongside other Leviticus references; this independently corroborates one USFX token without certifying equivalence of the full digital citation list.
The printed reference at Deuteronomy 19:15 cites Numbers 35:30, not the unaddressable eBible Numbers 35:50. Biblia's shortened digital note also cites 35:30.
The original 1910 printed marginal note beside Joshua 5:13 contains Ex. 23. 23., while both later digital apparatus labels say És 23:23.
The 1910 printed t marginal note at Joshua 14:6 cites Num. 14. 24. and De. 1. 36.; neither digital first target reproduces it.
The source chapter is 2 Chronicles 35; its printed g note uses contextual chapter 30.24, followed by Ezekiel 45.17. The printed first target belongs to 2 Chronicles, not 2 Kings.
On the original Isaiah 11 printed margin, the contextual x-reference reads 65.25; eBible changes the numeric destination to unattested Isa 65:26.
In the original printed Jeremiah 1 introductory chronology, the i-reference is 2 Kings 23:34, whereas both digital witnesses give a malformed 2 Kings 5 reference.
Jeremiah 32:29's printed context cites Jeremiah 21:10 within a longer marginal note, while eBible gives the nonexistent Jeremiah 21:20.
The original marginal r-reference at the account of Ishmael and Gedaliah cites 2 Kings 25:25; eBible gives nonexistent 2 Kings 25:35.
Matthew 12:40's printed Jonah reference uses the original-1910 Jonah 2:1 numbering; the two digital witnesses cite Jonah 1:17, a known alternate versification token.

The printed e note beside Jesus receiving the children includes an implicit Matthew 18:3, not the impossible Mark 18:3. The 1910 printed reference group also contains extra targets and differs in order; this records only the identified token.
The printed o note alongside Matthew 20:27 gives the contextual same-book reference Matthew 23:11. Both later digital hosts instead attribute 23:11 to Mark, which has no chapter 23.

The printed o marginal group for Luke 22:69 includes Mark 16:19 alongside Psalm 110:1 and Hebrews 1:3/8:1. Neither digital witness preserves this printed Mark destination; do not infer a complete note correspondence.
Romans 9:26 cites Hosea 2:1 in the printed margin rather than Hosea 1:10 in both digital witnesses. The passage is an established alternate-versification case.
Romans 10:15 contains a printed marginal Nahum 2:1 cross-reference, whereas both digital witnesses say Nahum 1:15. This is a verse-numbering difference, not permission to alter the source.
The printed prayer-related q reference beside 1 Thessalonians 3:10 spans Romans 1:10-12, unlike the two truncated/malformed digitized citations. This is a partial printed group reading.
The original first Thessalonians 4 fraternal-love context visibly cites 1 Peter 4:8 in the margin; two digital witnesses mistakenly cite 2 Peter with different chapter numbers.

The printed Isaiah 8:17-18 citation accompanies Hebrews 2:13's 'I will put my trust in him' quotation. Both digital variants instead present impossible Psalm 8:13 or Psalm 8:10 in this source's numbering; the printed sign and quotation relationship need preservation.
Hebrews 13:11 carries a printed Leviticus 4:12/21 and 16:27 parallel group. This differs in grouping from both digital `xt` labels; no entire-note equality is implied.

The printed reference beside 1 Peter 2:10 contains Hosea 2:1,25 in the 1910 page's numbering, whereas the digital witnesses use Hosea 1:10 and 2:22; this requires historical versification mapping, not silently invented targets.
The d marginal note near the 1 John 3:1 children-of-God passage explicitly reads Jn. 1. 12., not 1 Jn 1:12.

The original 1910 printed s reference beside sealing the servants reads Ez. 9. 4-6.; eBible and Biblia reference Ephesians, and the first digitization even cites a nonexistent Ephesians 9:4. Printed range details do not authorize creating a machine target without separate review.
